content:
Another week, another streaming service price hike. This week, ESPN announced that the monthly fees for ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited will increase, and some Disney+ and Hulu bundle plans will follow suit.

This price increase was discovered by sports media website Sports Media Watch from ESPN's support pages. The new rates will take effect on September 17. Here are the details of the price hike:

  • ESPN Select monthly fee: US$14 per month (originally US$13 per month)
  • ESPN Select annual fee: US$140 per year (originally US$130 per year)
  • ESPN Unlimited monthly fee: US$32 per month (originally US$30 per month)
  • ESPN Unlimited annual fee: US$320 per year (originally US$300 per year)

As reported, since ESPN overhauled its streaming strategy last year, this is the first price hike for these services.

On the other hand, some Disney+ bundle plans will also see fee increases to match the ESPN streaming service price hike.

  • Disney+ (with ads), Hulu (with ads) and ESPN Select: US$22 per month (originally US$20 per month)
  • Disney+ (no ads), Hulu (no ads) and ESPN Select: US$33 per month (originally US$30 per month)

As The Verge pointed out, this price hike also affects the existing ad-free Hulu, Disney+ and ESPN Select bundle, which is no longer accepting new subscribers. The monthly fee for this bundle will increase from US$25 to US$28.

The good news is: the ESPN Unlimited bundle was not affected by this price hike.

Peacock also announced a price increase last week, up to US$3 more per month or US$30 more per year. Apple has also recently raised prices for Apple Music and Apple One.
